office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, covering school funding, the tax structure, housing rules, and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Five-term Republican Mike Steele, the capital-budget ranking member, faces Democrat Maggie Adams, an IATSE union representative from Snoqualmie. Steele led the primary 41.1% to 33.9%; Adams led the King County portion.

candidates.summary: Incumbent since 2017, Capital Budget ranking member and Lake Chelan Chamber director, running on small-business, budget and infrastructure priorities.
highlights: Says taxes, fees and regulation make housing less affordable [S12]
Endorsed by the State Labor Council and WEA-PAC as well as AWB and the King County GOP [S3][S13][S14][S15]

taxes.basis: Voted against the 2026 income tax, campaigns on lowering tax burdens, and has said the state has a spending problem rather than a revenue problem.

spending.basis: Emphasizes balanced budgets and making sure every education dollar delivers results; describes a spending problem.

housing.basis: Said affordable housing cannot be made more affordable by more taxes, fees or unfavorable regulation.

safety.basis: Reported to oppose decriminalization; endorsed by the Fraternal Order of Police.

climate.basis: Opposes policies that would significantly raise transportation and energy costs; no direct climate statement.

experience.basis: Ten years in office with budget-committee seniority and past caucus leadership.

healthcare.basis: Wants to expand affordable options through transparency, choice and cost containment within the current system.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296 twice; his caucus site backs school choice and 'empowering parents.'

candidates.summary: IATSE Local 887 business representative from Snoqualmie, a first-time candidate running on healthcare access, workers' rights and water protection.
highlights: Calls healthcare "a fundamental human right" and wants comprehensive access statewide [S2]
Has said she supports a millionaire's tax [S7]
Supports term limits and lowering the voting age to 16 for state and local elections [S2]

taxes.basis: Has said she supports a millionaire's tax and higher taxes on high-grossing businesses; pamphlet lists tax fairness.

spending.basis: Wants better pay and facilities for educators and statewide healthcare access.

housing.basis: Would regulate vacation rentals and mandate affordable units in new construction.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with union leadership but no public office.

reform.basis: Supports constitutional term limits for elected offices and federal judges and voting at 16.

healthcare.basis: Calls healthcare a human right and wants comprehensive access everywhere, without naming single-payer.

tech.basis: Wants communities and farmers to have priority for water over incoming data centers.
